newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Gold is the only gleam in dull commodities.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gold is the only gleam in dull commodities.

text.p: Commodity markets with the possible exception of precious metals on Monday did not seem to be much of a lure for any money that came out of jittery equities or bonds.

Precious metals added modestly to Friday gains as dealers watched the dollar, Wall Street and the bond markets for further falls, traders said. "It is not entirely clear whether this was short covering or there was some fresh buying coming into gold on Friday," one analyst said as the London price was fixed at $327.70 per ounce.

This was up from $323.70 on Friday. "What was happening elsewhere played a major role in the gold market on Friday," said a participant, of the 156-point fall in the Dow and the losses by the dollar and the U.S. long bond.
But another dealer said that "if there is a reallocation of funds going on (from the stock markets into gold and elsewhere) it is difficult to know what these people's targets in gold would be".
Other commodity markets were mostly rangebound or easier.
Chicago new crop corn (maize) and soybean futures opened sharply lower on Monday after light, but much-needed rains fell across Illinois and Indiana over the weekend.
Forecasts called for heavier rains in dry pockets of the Corn Belt on Monday and Tuesday which contributed to the declines, they said.
Weather Services Corp predicted 0.50 to 1.50 inches of rain for Missouri, Illinois, Indiana and Ohio during the next 24 to 48 hours.
Portions of those states had been in dire need of moisture after an unusually dry month of July.
November soybeans were soon down 23-1/2 cents at $6.14 a bushel at the Chicago Board of Trade. Corn for December was down eight at $2.49. Wheat was also easier.
